root_cause.text: In the DMA error cleanup path of the e1000/e1000e TX mapping functions, the `count` variable, which already holds the correct number of successfully mapped buffers, was unnecessarily decremented before the unmap loop, causing an off-by-one error that leaks one DMA mapping.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the lines `if (count) count--;` from both `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000/e1000_main.c` and `drivers/net/ethernet/intel/e1000e/netdev.c` in the `dma_error` label, and the CVE description states: "Decrementing count before the while loop in dma_error causes an off-by-one error. If any mapping was successful before an unsuccessful mapping, exactly one DMA mapping would leak."

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix TX DMA error cleanup to properly unmap all previously mapped descriptors by removing the erroneous decrement of count.
intent_record.what: Removed the conditional decrement of count (if (count) count--;) at the dma_error label in e1000_tx_map.
intent_record.how: Previously, after a DMA mapping failure, count was decremented by one if non-zero before the cleanup loop, causing the loop to skip unmapping the last successfully mapped descriptor. Now count is left unchanged, so the loop unmaps all previously mapped descriptors.

intent_record.how: Previously, the code decremented 'count' by one (if non-zero) before entering a loop that unmaps DMA mappings. Now the loop uses the original 'count' value, ensuring all successful mappings are unmapped.
